# Risk Policy: Potential Indicators and Pathways

::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
Risk policy is a Council-level decision. Current [Risk Policy](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2020/12/15/2020-27562/fisheries-of-the-northeastern-united-states-omnibus-framework-adjustment-to-modify-the-mid-atlantic) uses stock status as the only indicator of when to adjust risk tolerance. Low stock status (B/Bmsy < 1) results in much more risk averse probability of overfishing and lower ABC relative to OFL, high stock status (>1.5 B/Bmsy) is as risk tolerant as allowed by law with ABC close to OFL. 
:::

*  **Key question: What additional indicators could inform Council risk tolerance? Could habitat conditions or socioeconomic indicators in addition to stock status tell us whether we can be more or less risky?** 
  
*  **Scope:  Should we develop a general process for using indicators in the risk policy, or focus on a specific application for a single species? Which species?**

:::::: {.cols data-latex=""}

::: {.col data-latex="{0.49\textwidth}"}
::: {.ltbluebox data-latex=""}
## What information is used now?

The current Risk Policy was finalized by the Council in [December 2020](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2020/12/15/2020-27562/fisheries-of-the-northeastern-united-states-omnibus-framework-adjustment-to-modify-the-mid-atlantic). It is based on a [management strategy evaluation](https://static1.squarespace.com/static/511cdc7fe4b00307a2628ac6/t/5e56e0f286208b151ba4f55d/1582752007474/S1_Fine+tuning+the+ABC+control+rule+for+Mid-Atlantic+stocks_Wiedenmann.pdf) that compared performance of alternative policies across life history types represented by summer flounder, scup, and butterfish. 

\vspace{1ex}

```{r MAFMCriskpolicy, fig.asp = 0.7}

riskpol <- data.frame(Bfrac = c(0, 0.1, 1.0, 1.5, 2.5),
                      Current = c(0, 0, 0.45, 0.49, 0.49),
                      Pre2020 = c(0, 0, 0.4, 0.4, 0.4)
)

riskpol <- riskpol |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-Bfrac, names_to = "pstar")

p1 <- ggplot2::ggplot(riskpol, ggplot2::aes(x=Bfrac, y=value, linetype = pstar)) +
  ggplot2::geom_path(show.legend = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  ggplot2::xlab("B/Bmsy") +
  ggplot2::ylab("p*") +
  ggplot2::labs(linetype = "Policy")#+
  #theme(legend.position="bottom")

p1
#print(p1, vp=grid::viewport(gp=grid::gpar(cex=1.5)))
```

\vspace{1ex}

The [ABC control rule](http://www.mafmc.org/s/MAFMC-ABC-Control-Rule-White-Paper.pdf) includes an SSC decision on uncertainty in the assessment and converts the risk policy into an ABC given the stock status.

```{r OFLCVtoABC, fig.asp = 0.7}

ABCprop <- data.frame(Bfrac = seq(0, 2.5, 0.01)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pstar = dplyr::case_when(Bfrac <= 0.1 ~ 0,
                                  Bfrac > 0.1 & Bfrac <= 1.0 ~ (Bfrac-0.1)*((0.45-0)/(1-0.1)) ,
                                  Bfrac > 1.0 & Bfrac <= 1.5 ~ (Bfrac-1.0)*((0.49-0.45)/(1.5-1))+0.45,
                                  Bfrac > 1.5 ~ 0.49)) |>
  dplyr::mutate("CV=60%" = qlnorm(pstar, log(1), log(0.60 + 1)),
                "CV=100%" = qlnorm(pstar, log(1), log(1.00 + 1)),
                "CV=150%" = qlnorm(pstar, log(1), log(1.50 + 1))) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(Bfrac, pstar), names_to = "CVlevel")
                       

p2 <- ggplot2::ggplot(ABCprop, ggplot2::aes(x=Bfrac, y=value, colour=CVlevel)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line()+  
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  ggplot2::xlab("B/Bmsy") +
  ggplot2::ylab("ABC/OFL proportion") +
  ggplot2::labs(colour = "OFL CV") #+
  #theme(legend.position="bottom")

p2
#print(p2, vp=grid::viewport(gp=grid::gpar(cex=1.5)))
  
```

::: {.ltpurplebox data-latex=""}
**Important:** The use of indicators in the SSC's ABC decision process will be **considered separately** under Catch/Quota setting. Indicators here will address the risk policy and adjustment to risk tolerance rather than assessment uncertainty.
:::

## Information sources for indicators

### Potential Indicator Sources



[Ecosystem and Socioeconomic Profiles](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/new-england-mid-atlantic/ecosystems/ecosystem-and-socioeconomic-profile-development-and-reports) conceptual models and indicators for MAFMC stocks: 

*  Black Sea Bass
*  Bluefish 
*  Golden Tilefish
*  Longfin squid 
*  Shortfin squid

[State of the Ecosystem](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/new-england-mid-atlantic/ecosystems/state-ecosystem-reports-northeast-us-shelf) and [Risk Assessment](https://www.mafmc.org/s/2_MAB_RiskAssess_2024.pdf) indicators

### Potential Pathways
*  Evaluate indicators of favorable or unfavorable habitat or socioeconomic conditions for a species or life history type
*  Simulate management with different risk tolerance under different conditions (update MSE?)
*  Compare indicator-based approach vs. status quo: Which indicator-adjusted risk tolerance meets objectives across species portfolio or for a selected individual species?

## Information gaps 

Ecosystem and Socioeconomic Profiles do not yet exist for the species originally used to evaluate the Risk Policy: summer flounder, scup, and butterfish.
